questions.stem: According to the passage, what did scientists do to test the real-life effects of the human NOVA1 variant?
options: They compared the brains of humans and Neanderthals directly.
They used CRISPR gene editing to replace the NOVA1 protein in mice with the human version.
They studied speech disorders in British children.
They analyzed fossils of early human throats.
questions.evidence: The latest research involved scientists using CRISPR gene editing methods to replace the NOVA1 protein found in mice with the one found in humans.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에서 연구자들이 CRISPR 유전자 편집을 이용해 쥐의 NOVA1 단백질을 인간 버전으로 교체했다고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.stem: All of the following are mentioned in the passage as findings related to NOVA1 or FOXP2 EXCEPT:
options: Baby mice with the human NOVA1 variant made different sounds when their mother approached.
Adult male mice with the human NOVA1 variant made different sounds near a female they wanted to mate with.
The NOVA1 variant in modern humans is found only in humans, not other species.
The FOXP2 variant in modern humans is found only in humans, not shared with Neanderthals.
questions.evidence: Later research found it was shared with Neanderthals.
questions.explanation_ko: FOXP2 변이는 네안데르탈인과도 공유된다고 나와 있으므로, '인간에게만 있다'는 진술은 사실이 아닙니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about why NOVA1 might explain a unique human advantage over Neanderthals and Denisovans?
options: Because NOVA1 is only found in the human species, unlike FOXP2 which was shared with Neanderthals.
Because Neanderthals and Denisovans had larger brains than humans.
Because Neanderthals could not produce any sounds at all.
Because FOXP2 was never found in any species besides humans.
questions.evidence: The NOVA1 variant in modern humans, on the other hand, is found only in our species, Darnell said.
questions.explanation_ko: NOVA1은 인간에게만 존재하지만 FOXP2는 네안데르탈인과 공유되었다는 점에서, NOVA1이 인간만의 고유한 언어적 이점을 설명할 수 있다는 추론이 가능합니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention the earlier discovery of the FOXP2 gene?
options: To show that FOXP2 is more important than NOVA1 for speech development.
To contrast it with NOVA1, since FOXP2 was shared with Neanderthals while NOVA1 is unique to humans.
To prove that gene editing was first used in 2001.
To explain how FOXP2 causes hearing loss in humans.
questions.evidence: But even though FOXP2 was found to be linked to human language, the variant in modern humans was not found in our species alone.
questions.explanation_ko: 저자는 FOXP2와 NOVA1을 비교하여 NOVA1이 인간에게만 있다는 점을 강조하기 위해 FOXP2를 언급합니다.

questions.stem: In the sentence "Darnell told the AP the genetic version, or variant, included the protein that helped humans develop into the 'dominant species' that remains today," what does "dominant species" most likely mean?
options: The species with the most advanced physical strength.
The species that has the greatest influence and control compared to others.
The species that reproduces the fastest.
The species that lives in the widest variety of climates.
questions.evidence: Darnell told the AP the genetic version, or variant, included the protein that helped humans develop into the “ dominant species ” that remains today.
questions.explanation_ko: 'dominant species'는 다른 종들보다 더 강한 영향력과 통제력을 가진 종을 의미합니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 예를 들어, 말은 개인들이 정보를 공유하고, 활동을 조직하고, 지식을 물려주는 것을 가능하게 했습니다.
다넬은 그 유전적 변이가 오늘날까지 남아있는 '우세종'으로 인간이 발전하는 데 도움을 준 단백질을 포함하고 있다고 AP에 말했습니다.
최근 연구는 과학자들이 CRISPR 유전자 편집 방법을 사용하여 쥐에서 발견된 NOVA1 단백질을 인간에게서 발견된 것으로 교체하는 것을 포함했습니다.
2001년에 영국 과학자들은 언어 및 말하기 장애와 관련된 최초의 유전자를 발견했다고 발표했습니다.
연구자들은 그 변이가 동물들이 서로에게 소리를 내는 방식을 바꾸었다는 것을 알고 놀랐습니다.

key_points: A study links a human-specific protein called NOVA1 to the development of speech.
Scientists used CRISPR to replace NOVA1 in mice with the human variant and found it changed how the mice vocalized.
Baby mice and adult male mice with the human variant made different sounds in situations involving their mother or a potential mate.
The NOVA1 variant is found only in humans, unlike the earlier-discovered FOXP2 gene, which was shared with Neanderthals.
Speech ability also depends on physical structures like the throat and brain regions, not genetics alone.
Researchers hope this discovery could help treat speech-related problems and identify children who need early language support.
main_idea: A new study suggests that a human-specific gene variant called NOVA1 may have played a key role in the development of human speech, giving early humans an advantage over related species like Neanderthals.
restate_sentence: The researchers were surprised to learn that the variant changed the way the animals called out to each other.
